title: ENGR 500 B - How to Use the Engineering Courses

quizzes.title: What These Courses Are, and What They Are Not

questions.q: What does the lecture say the Engineering courses provide? [1.1]
options: Engineering knowledge, not a qualification to practise
questions.explain:
Paragraph 1.1: They sit entirely on the knowledge side of the boundary.
B is wrong: No licence comes from these courses.
C is wrong: That can only happen on the job.
D is wrong: The courses grant no degree.

questions.q: Which kind of work does the lecture say belongs with qualified professionals? [1.3]
options: Electrical work, gas lines, structural changes and pressure systems
questions.explain:
Paragraph 1.3: These are named as safety-critical work for professionals under local codes.
B is wrong: Reading is exactly what the courses are for.
C is wrong: Quizzes are part of the course.
D is wrong: Lecture six treats these as reasonable projects.

questions.q: Why can a correct textbook calculation still lead to a wrong design? [1.4]
options: Real materials have flaws, loads are uncertain and codes add margins learned from failures
questions.explain:
Paragraph 1.4: Knowing about a thing differs from doing it safely.
A is wrong: Codes guide design; they do not forbid calculation.
B is wrong: Mathematics is central to engineering.
D is wrong: The lecture says the calculation can be correct.

questions.q: What mental model does the lecture recommend for holding what you learn? [1.8]
options: A licence to do your own wiring
A second opinion to overrule professionals
The knowledge behind a conversation with an engineer or tradesperson, not a replacement for them
questions.explain:
Paragraph 1.8: Their years of applying knowledge under codes are what you rely on.
A is wrong: The courses give no such right.
B is wrong: The model is understanding, not overruling.
C is wrong: Each course is only a careful first hour.

questions.q: How does a Brief course compare with a real university course on the same subject? [1.9]
options: It covers the same material in full
It is a careful first hour, while the real course fills a semester of well over a hundred hours
It is longer and more detailed
questions.explain:
Paragraph 1.9: Brief courses give main ideas, key vocabulary and a map onward.
A is wrong: Laboratories cannot be replaced online.
B is wrong: It covers only the main ideas.
D is wrong: The real course is far longer.

quizzes.title: Where the Courses Come From: MIT and OpenCourseWare

questions.q: What is MIT's motto, and what does it mean? [2.2]
options: Scientia potentia est: knowledge is power
Mens et Manus: mind and hand
Lux et Veritas: light and truth
questions.explain:
Paragraph 2.2: Theory and practice belong together.
A is wrong: That is Harvard's motto.
B is wrong: Not MIT's motto.
D is wrong: That is Yale's motto.

questions.q: Which MIT Course number is Electrical Engineering and Computer Science? [2.3]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 2.3: An MIT student might say, I am Course 6.
B is wrong: That is Nuclear Science and Engineering.
C is wrong: That is Mechanical Engineering.
D is wrong: That is Civil and Environmental Engineering.

questions.q: In the subject number 18.01, what does the 18 tell you? [2.4]
options: The year it was first taught
questions.explain:
Paragraph 2.4: The number after the point identifies the subject.
A is wrong: It names the department.
B is wrong: The number is not a date.
D is wrong: The number is not a count.

questions.q: What is true of MIT's structure beyond the General Institute Requirements? [2.5]
options: Students choose any subjects with no requirements
All engineers take the same ten core subjects
There is no single engineering core; each department sets its own required subjects
questions.explain:
Paragraph 2.5: The GIRs are the only Institute-wide core.
A is wrong: Each department has requirements.
B is wrong: No such shared core exists.
C is wrong: Every department sets its own.

questions.q: How does the Academy use MIT's curriculum and OpenCourseWare? [2.7]
options: As a map: titles and order follow MIT, but the lectures are written fresh
It is an official MIT partner
It ignores MIT once titles are chosen
questions.explain:
Paragraph 2.7: Nothing is copied, and there is no connection with MIT.
B is wrong: The Academy has no connection with MIT.
C is wrong: The open materials help decide what each course covers.
D is wrong: OCW's licence forbids commercial reuse, and nothing is copied.

questions.q: What does ABET do? [3.2]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 3.2: It checks that programs meet its standards.
A is wrong: OCW is run by MIT.
C is wrong: That is NCEES.
D is wrong: State boards issue licences.

questions.q: Why do the Foundations courses come first? [3.3]
options: The first two years of an engineering degree are built on mathematics and science
questions.explain:
Paragraph 3.3: They match MIT's General Institute Requirements.
A is wrong: Order follows the degree, not ease.
B is wrong: They prepare for them.
C is wrong: No law is involved.

questions.q: What does passing the FE exam earn? [3.6]
options: The title Engineer in Training, or Engineer Intern
questions.explain:
Paragraph 3.6: On the road to a licence, but not yet licensed.
B is wrong: The degree comes from the program.
C is wrong: Only licensed engineers can.
D is wrong: That needs experience and the PE exam.

questions.q: What does it mean for a licensed engineer to seal drawings? [3.8]
options: They formally take legal responsibility for them
They hand responsibility to the contractor
questions.explain:
Paragraph 3.8: Sealing is a sign of accountability.
B is wrong: The opposite is true.
C is wrong: Not the meaning given.
D is wrong: Not the meaning given.

questions.q: Which engineers usually do not need a licence? [3.9]
options: Many engineers inside companies and most software engineers
questions.explain:
Paragraph 3.9: State law usually does not require it for their work.
B is wrong: Work offered to the public needs a licensed engineer.
C is wrong: Same: public works need a licensed engineer.
D is wrong: Licences are required for public work.

quizzes.title: A Tour of the Engineering Library

questions.q: What do the five hundreds in Engineering course numbers signal? [4.2]
options: A separate library that comes after the undergraduate courses numbered 100 to 499
They are the hardest undergraduate courses
questions.explain:
Paragraph 4.2: Engineering 500 B is Course Zero.
B is wrong: The numbering is deliberate.
C is wrong: They form a separate library.
D is wrong: MIT uses numbers like 18.01.

questions.q: Which course is Engineering 501 B? [4.3]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 4.3: The first Foundations course.
B is wrong: That is Engineering 503 B.
C is wrong: That is Engineering 506 B.
D is wrong: That is Engineering 508 B.

questions.q: Why does Engineering 506 B teach biology? [4.4]
options: Every MIT student, engineer or not, studies biology
questions.explain:
Paragraph 4.4: Biology is one of the six science GIRs.
A is wrong: It is an Engineering Foundations course.
B is wrong: Chemistry is a separate course, 505 B.
C is wrong: Every MIT student takes it.

questions.q: How does the Academy handle the humanities requirement? [4.5]
options: It adds humanities lectures to every course
questions.explain:
Paragraph 4.5: You are encouraged to take courses there alongside engineering.
B is wrong: Laboratories cannot be given online.
C is wrong: It is already served elsewhere.
D is wrong: Not described.

questions.q: When will the department courses get their course numbers? [4.8]
options: Never; they will not be built
questions.explain:
Paragraph 4.8: Foundations first, then the departments.
A is wrong: They are part of the plan.
B is wrong: Numbers are assigned later.
C is wrong: The plan is Foundations first.

quizzes.title: How to Study Engineering the Way Engineers Do

questions.q: What is the first method for learning engineering? [5.2]
options: Work problems by hand before looking at the answer
Read worked solutions until they feel familiar
questions.explain:
Paragraph 5.2: The struggle is where learning happens.
B is wrong: Familiarity is not the same as understanding.
C is wrong: Answers alone teach little.
D is wrong: Not described.

questions.q: In the standard problem routine, when do you put in the numbers? [5.3]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 5.3: Then check units, size and behaviour.
B is wrong: The sketch comes early.
C is wrong: Numbers come at the end.
D is wrong: Symbols come first.

questions.q: Why was the Mars Climate Orbiter lost in 1999? [5.4]
options: It was hit by a meteor
One piece of software used pound-force seconds while another expected newton-seconds
questions.explain:
Paragraph 5.4: A unit mismatch sent it too close to Mars.
A is wrong: Not the cause described.
B is wrong: Not the cause described.
D is wrong: Not the cause described.

questions.q: What is a back-of-the-envelope estimate for? [5.5]
options: A final answer for a design
A note to post to an engineer
A rough guess to the nearest power of ten that shows when a careful calculation has gone wrong
A way to avoid calculating at all
questions.explain:
Paragraph 5.5: One of the most useful engineering skills.
A is wrong: It is a check, not a design.
B is wrong: Not the meaning given.
D is wrong: It comes before the calculation.

questions.q: What is the firm rule for using an AI tutor? [5.11]
options: Trust it whenever it sounds confident
Use it to approve changes to your house
Use it to learn engineering, not to certify designs
questions.explain:
Paragraph 5.11: Real decisions belong with a qualified engineer.
A is wrong: AI is encouraged as a tutor.
B is wrong: It can make confident errors.
C is wrong: That is an engineering decision for a professional.

questions.q: Which question does the lecture suggest asking a professional about a project? [6.3]
options: What loads is this designed for?
Why do you need a licence?
Can I do the structural work myself?
Can you skip the code to save money?
questions.explain:
Paragraph 6.3: One of several good questions listed.
B is wrong: Not suggested.
C is wrong: Lecture six advises against it.
D is wrong: Not suggested.

questions.q: Which principle exposes perpetual motion machines? [6.4]
options: Machines always get faster over time
Energy is never created from nothing
questions.explain:
Paragraph 6.4: Every real machine also loses energy to friction and heat.
A is wrong: A claim needs independent measured data.
B is wrong: Not true.
C is wrong: Every real machine loses energy.

questions.q: What caused the Hyatt Regency walkway collapse in 1981? [6.6]
options: Too many people for a correct design
A change to how the walkways hung from their rods roughly doubled the load on a connection
questions.explain:
Paragraph 6.6: The change was not properly checked; 114 people died.
A is wrong: Not the cause described.
B is wrong: The design change was the cause.
D is wrong: Not the cause described.

questions.q: What does the NSPE code of ethics ask engineers to hold paramount? [6.7]
options: The safety, health and welfare of the public
questions.explain:
Paragraph 6.7: Public safety comes above all.
B is wrong: Not mentioned.
C is wrong: Not the first duty.
D is wrong: Not mentioned.

questions.q: Which courses does the lecture suggest taking next? [6.9]
options: Engineering 501 B, Calculus I, alongside Engineering 503 B, Physics I
questions.explain:
Paragraph 6.9: Then follow the numbers through the Foundations.
A is wrong: That begins the medical library.
B is wrong: The Foundations come first.
D is wrong: The library is a work in progress.
